summary: Live validation completed against a fresh output directory. The repaired workflow now honestly produces scene_off_flashlight_off as a no-flashlight-ever control in metadata, but the rendered image is still broadly lit, so the user's scene-off brightness/flicker problem is not solved by the baseline-leakage repair alone. The remaining brightness is now attributable to residual environment/static/material lighting or renderer state, not to prior flashlight warm-up leakage.
work_completed: Confirmed examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation_after_fix did not exist before validation, avoiding stale frame mixing.

Ran the requested workflow. The default python invocation failed because the base environment lacked the spear package and OpenCV; reran the same workflow with --python /home/yashturkar/miniconda3/envs/spear-env/bin/python and completed successfully.

Generated fresh outputs for scene_on_flashlight_off, scene_on_flashlight_on, scene_off_flashlight_off, and scene_off_flashlight_on under examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation_after_fix.
Computed RGB luma, p99 luma, bright-pixel percentages, off/on deltas, loop-closure deltas, depth equality, MP4 readability, and metadata diagnostics for all four settings.
Visually inspected representative scene_off_flashlight_off and scene_off_flashlight_on frames.

findings.message: scene_off_flashlight_off is no-flashlight-ever but is not dark. Metadata reports render_diagnostics.no_flashlight_ever_control=true, initial_light_setup.command=null, spawn_flashlight=false, flashlight_ever_spawned_after_setting_setup=false, and flashlight_ever_enabled_after_setting_setup=false. Despite that, RGB luma remains high: mean min/median/max 118.795/136.006/151.054, frame_0000 mean 135.886, p99 median 224.367, and >=230 luma pixels median 0.0755%. Representative frame: examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation_after_fix/scene_off_flashlight_off/frames/rgb/frame_0000.png.

The live rerender does not solve the reported scene-off brightness problem. The new scene_off_flashlight_off luma is effectively unchanged from the prior failed output, whose median mean luma was 136.080 versus 136.006 after the fix. Because the new metadata proves no flashlight was ever spawned/enabled for this control, remaining brightness is residual environment/static/material illumination or renderer state rather than baseline flashlight warm-up leakage.

scene_off_flashlight_on shows a flashlight contribution, but only on top of an already bright scene-off baseline. Compared with scene_off_flashlight_off, median mean luma rises only 3.360, while p99 rises from 224.367 to 246.914 and newly >=230-luma pixels are 5.874% median. Positive luma delta >20 affects 10.450% of pixels median and >40 affects 5.402% median, consistent with a local highlight/beam region rather than pure global accumulation, but the validation is still not flashlight-only because the baseline is bright.

Render-history metadata is honest but not verified. Each metadata.json has disable_render_history=true and render_history_disable_verified=false. deterministic_capture says render-history disable was requested but live proxy readback did not verify every component, with unverified_render_history_components ['rgb', 'depth_meters']; property readbacks are null and always_persist_rendering_state_disabled=false for both capture components.

Temporal/render instability remains visible at the same orbit pose. Frame_0000 to frame_0239 mean absolute luma deltas are 8.149 for scene_off_flashlight_off and 4.825 for scene_off_flashlight_on, with 54.36% and 32.95% of pixels changing by >5 luma respectively. scene_on_flashlight_on is much cleaner at 1.196 mean absolute luma and 3.83% >5.

Fresh output completeness checks passed: each setting has 240 RGB PNGs, 240 depth NPY frames, 240 viridis depth PNGs, readable 240-frame RGB MP4 at 24 FPS and 1280x720, plus metadata.json. Raw depth frames are byte-identical across all four settings for all 240 frames.

Scene light metadata shows the script disabled/zeroed 8 light components for scene-off and hid 1 USkyLightComponent, but environment_contributors.properties_zeroed remains 0. This supports residual environment/static/material lighting as the next root-cause area.

The successful render process returned exit code 0, but logs emitted 'ERROR: Unexpected frame state: request_begin_next_frame' during group teardown before closing Unreal instances. Outputs were complete and readable, so this did not block validation.

follow_up_recommendations: Builder should repair the remaining scene-off illumination source in the map/render environment: eliminate or black out emissive/static-lit materials, verify skylight/environment intensity is actually zeroed, and use a no-baked-lighting flashlight-only validation map if needed.
Builder should make render-history disabling verifiable or fail fast when deterministic capture cannot confirm rgb/depth_meters capture components.
After environment repair, rerun the same fresh-output validation and require scene_off_flashlight_off median mean luma to be near black before interpreting scene_off_flashlight_on as flashlight-only.
memory_worthy: Live validation after the orbit baseline leakage fix shows scene_off_flashlight_off is now a true no-flashlight-ever control in metadata, but it remains bright at median mean luma about 136, so the remaining scene-off brightness is environment/static/material lighting or renderer state rather than baseline flashlight warm-up leakage.
